newsitem.title: UK: US bank analyst upbeat on upcoming Russia Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: US bank analyst upbeat on upcoming Russia Eurobond.

text.p: Russia's long-awaited debut Eurobond will be a key event in establishing a benchmark for future Russian borrowers, Eric Fine, East European bond strategist at Morgan Stanley, said on Tuesday.
"This is an extremely important event and is just the starting gun," he told Reuters Financial Television. "It will establish a benchmark for future Russian issuance from the corporate sector."
In line to follow are the cities of Moscow and St Petersburg and Gazprom, the world's largest natural gas producer.
It will be the first time Russia has accessed the international capital markets for almost 80 years, since the 1917 revolution.
The bond is expected to be for up to $500 million and mature after five-years. Russia believes it may pay 10 to 11 percent for the issue, a senior finance ministry official said today.
Fine told RFTV: "It will be (launched at) a fair spread, around 350 to 375 basis points over U.S. Treasuries."
He said this was a reasonable spread as Mexico, with a slightly stronger rating, trades at around 310 b.p. over and Argentina, with a slightly weaker rating, at around 370 b.p.
Other analysts have estimated a more generous ceiling of up to 400 b.p. over Treasuries for Russia's Eurobond.
Russia is rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB minus by Standard & Poor's Corp.
Fine said many different types of investors would buy Russia's Eurobond.
"Banks will buy it for their retail clients and own books, as will dedicated emerging market and general fixed income funds that need their slice of Russia," Fine said.
He said while there was a lot of demand for Russia, the existing assets did not permit all investors to participate.
"But a five-year Eurobond should be acceptable to a much broader investor class," he said.
Russia will issue the Eurobond between November 21 and 25, Finance Minister Alexander Livshits has said previously.

The country began a series of top level economic presentations around the world on Monday. Three teams of finance ministry and central bank officials were accompanied by the joint lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg.
Today, teams visited Seoul, Geneva and Zurich.
"This is the starting bell of a regular issuer on the international capital markets," Fine said.
